name: IIT Bombay
pros: Extremely strong coding and startup culture
Prime location in Mumbai with excellent industry connects
Highly prestigious alumni network and funding opportunities
cons: Extremely competitive and high-pressure peer environment
Older hostel infrastructure in some blocks
campusVibe: An energetic, ambitious, and slightly overwhelming atmosphere. Students are constantly building, participating in hackathons, and preparing for competitive programming or finance roles.
codingCultureReview: World-class. The competitive programming culture is intense, and the student-led clubs are heavily backed by tech giants.
placementReality: Top-tier packages, especially for quant, HFT, and software roles. However, the competition among peers for Day 1 companies is cut-throat.
hostelReview: A mix of very old and newly built hostels. Space can be constrained, but the hostel culture is deeply bonding.
peerCompetitiveness: Very High. You are surrounded by the top 1% of the country.
attendanceStrictness: Moderate. Professors expect attendance, but the real learning often happens in clubs and project groups.
cityLife: Mumbai offers an unmatched cosmopolitan experience, though living outside campus can be expensive.
startupCulture: Unmatched in India. SINE (incubator) is highly active, and finding co-founders is very easy.
facultyQuality: Exceptional, with many professors heavily involved in industry consulting and cutting-edge research.
aiRecommendation: Best for extremely ambitious students aiming for top-tier software, quant, or startup founder roles.

name: IIT Delhi
pros: Excellent startup ecosystem and proximity to policy/tech hubs
Strong placement records in tech, finance, and consulting
Vibrant campus life with huge cultural fests
cons: Academic curriculum is notoriously rigorous and grading can be tough
Air quality in Delhi during winters can be a concern
campusVibe: Fast-paced and highly entrepreneurial. There's a strong focus on not just engineering, but also consulting, finance, and policy.
codingCultureReview: Very strong, though slightly more balanced with hardware and startup focus compared to other top IITs.
placementReality: Outstanding. Almost all major tech and consulting firms visit. High median packages.
hostelReview: Hostels are decent but often crowded. The mess food is average, but the surrounding areas (Hauz Khas) offer great options.
peerCompetitiveness: High. The academic pressure is significant due to tough grading curves.
attendanceStrictness: High. A 75% attendance rule is strictly enforced in many courses.
cityLife: Excellent. Located in the heart of South Delhi with great connectivity and access to culture/food.
startupCulture: Phenomenal. Delhi NCR is a massive startup hub, and IITD alumni are heavily represented.
facultyQuality: Top-notch, heavily focused on deep-tech research.
aiRecommendation: Ideal for students seeking a balance of elite tech placements and strong startup/consulting exposure.

name: IIT Madras
pros: Best engineering research ecosystem in India
Strong focus on deep tech and core engineering
cons: Food and weather might require adjustment for North Indian students
campusVibe: More laid-back socially but intensely rigorous academically. The campus is a dense forest with deer and monkeys, offering a unique serene environment.
codingCultureReview: Strong, but with a heavier emphasis on research, AI/ML, and deep tech compared to pure competitive programming.
placementReality: Stellar placements across IT, analytics, and core engineering. Very strong in R&D roles.
hostelReview: Hostels are reasonably good. The campus is massive, so bicycles are a must.
peerCompetitiveness: High academically, but the student community is generally collaborative.
attendanceStrictness: Strict. Academic discipline is highly valued here.
cityLife: Chennai is a major tech hub, though the campus itself is self-sufficient.
startupCulture: Very strong, especially for deep-tech, hardware, and SaaS startups via the IITM Research Park.
facultyQuality: Arguably the best in India for core engineering and research.
aiRecommendation: Best for students interested in deep tech, research, or a slightly calmer but academically rigorous environment.

name: DTU
pros: Massive tech placement numbers and strong alumni network
cons: Very large batch sizes mean high internal competition
Infrastructure is good but feels crowded
campusVibe: Very lively, practical, and highly focused on placements and coding. The 'chill' factor is higher here compared to IITs.
codingCultureReview: Excellent. The entire campus revolves around LeetCode, CP, and development. Huge peer-learning network.
placementReality: Top tech companies hire in large numbers. However, you must stand out among a very large batch.
hostelReview: Hostels are decent but securing one can be tough for Delhi residents due to limited capacity.
peerCompetitiveness: High for placements, but relaxed for academics.
attendanceStrictness: Lenient. Students get plenty of time to focus on coding and skills.
cityLife: Delhi location offers great exposure and connectivity.
startupCulture: Growing rapidly, with many successful tech startups emerging recently.
facultyQuality: Good, but the primary learning source is often peer groups.
aiRecommendation: Excellent ROI for coding-focused students who want strong tech placements without extreme academic pressure.
